raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--strip-thinking-cache`, a request that is retracted after it produced reasoning tokens corrupts KV accounting once it is re-prefilled: finishing it trips an assert in the radix cache, and a second retraction frees slots the tree still owns, so one `alloc()` can later hand a slot to two requests. Decode retracts whenever the KV pool runs out, so long reasoning outputs under memory pressure reach this.

Cause: `owned_kv_len()` returns the prompt length once a request has reasoning tokens, so `release_kv_cache` frees everything past the prompt as over-allocated. A retracted request keeps its output and is re-prefilled over `prompt + output`; that re-prefill's `checkpoint_kv_cache` puts the output into the tree (or its match already finds it there), so `cache_protected_len > prompt`. Finishing then trips the `cache_protected_len <= len(new_indices) + page_size - 1` assert in `UnifiedRadixCache.checkpoint_into_tree`, and a second retraction frees `[prompt, cache_protected_len)`; evicting the node frees those slots again.

Fixes #41617.

## Modifications

`Req.owned_kv_len()`, strip-thinking branch: `min(committed, max(len(origin_input_ids), cache_protected_len))`. Without a retraction `cache_protected_len <= prompt`, so nothing changes and the output is still stripped.

Capping the re-prefill's checkpoint at the prompt does not replace this floor: when the match already passes the prompt the capped checkpoint trips the same assert. Keeping a re-prefill's thinking tokens out of the tree is a follow-up on top of this floor.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_strip_thinking_after_retraction.py` (new, CPU, real `UnifiedRadixCache`, `checkpoint_kv_cache`, `release_kv_cache` and `evict`, with the flag on for the whole request) covers finish after a re-prefill, a second retraction, the no-retraction case (output still stripped), a chunked re-prefill whose first chunk ends inside the earlier output, a re-prefill whose match already passes the prompt, and page_size=4 with an aligned and an unaligned prompt. After release no tree-owned slot is in the free list (page_size 1), and after evicting the whole tree the free list has no duplicates and equals the pool.

Run on CPU: on main every retraction case fails (2 tests and 8 of 8 subtests; the no-retraction test passes). With the fix: 6 passed, 8 subtests passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit
- [x] Unit tests added

Developed with AI assistance (Claude); every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run locally by me.

nodes.body: Thanks for porting and running it, @ischencheng. I'm moving the tests to current main and will push the merge and answer the cap question in detail.

I merged main (no force-push) and ported the tests to `checkpoint_kv_cache`, `release_kv_cache(checkpoint=...)` and `TreeLock`, with the flag on for the whole request. On CPU I get the same result as you: without the fix the finish case trips the `cache_protected_len` assert and a second retraction frees [9..14]; with it, all pass. I also added a chunked re-prefill and a re-prefill whose match already passes the prompt.

You're right that thinking tokens shouldn't stay cached after a re-prefill, and with the original four tests the cap does pass, as you found. I'll add it as a follow-up. On its own it can't replace the floor, though: when the match already passes the prompt (now one of the tests), a capped `up_to` below `cache_protected_len` trips the same assert. On a mamba tree it can key the post-thinking state under the prompt.

The cap is built, as one commit on top of this branch, with a test. With `--strip-thinking-cache` and `reasoning_tokens > 0`, `checkpoint_kv_cache` now stops a re-prefill's checkpoint at the prompt, so the earlier thinking and answer tokens no longer go into the tree:

```python
up_to = req.extend_end
if (
    get_serving().strip_thinking_cache
    and req.reasoning_tokens > 0
    and not tree_cache.supports_mamba()
):
    up_to = min(up_to, max(len(req.origin_input_ids), req.kv.cache_protected_len))
```

The new case re-prefills a retracted request, plain and chunked, and checks that nothing past the prompt is matchable: on this PR's head it fails with `14 != 8`, and with the cap the file gives 7 passed, 10 subtests passed. The floor in `owned_kv_len()` stays: when the re-prefill's match already passes the prompt, the cap can't go below `cache_protected_len`, and with the cap but without the floor that case still trips the assert on finish (`cache_protected_len=12, len(new_indices)=8`) and a second retraction frees tree slots [9..12]. It skips mamba trees, where the live recurrent state is the state after the whole re-prefill: on CPU, a capped checkpoint stores that post-thinking state under the prompt node once the node's own state has been evicted. The branch is `sohom-cs:fix/strip-thinking-cap-reprefill-checkpoint`. I'll open it as a follow-up PR once this one merges, or push it here if you'd rather review both together.
ran the tests on CPU against current main, details inline.

needs a rebase, `cache_unfinished_req` is gone on main (it's `checkpoint_kv_cache(req, tree)` now). ported this test to main 70f0b7351e: without the fix the finish case now hits the `cache_protected_len <= len(new_indices) + page_size - 1` assert in `UnifiedRadixCache.checkpoint`, so it's a crash rather than a silent double free, and the second retraction still frees [9..14]. with your one-liner on top, all 4 pass.

@@ -0,0 +1,238 @@
+"""--strip-thinking-cache caps Req.owned_kv_len() at the prompt. A retracted
+request is re-prefilled over prompt + output, and the tree then holds part of
+that output (the re-prefill's checkpoint inserts it, or its match finds it), so
+cache_protected_len > prompt. Releasing it must never free those tree-owned
+slots: no slot may be free twice, and every slot must come back."""
+
+import contextlib
+import unittest
+from array import array
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import FINISH_LENGTH, Req  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator import TokenToKVPoolAllocator  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.paged import (  # noqa: E402
+    PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import EvictParams  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.cache_init_params import CacheInitParams  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.common import (  # noqa: E402
+    checkpoint_kv_cache,
+    release_kv_cache,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import (  # noqa: E402
+    MHATokenToKVPool,
+    ReqToTokenPool,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.components.base import (  # noqa: E402
+    ComponentType,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedRadixCache  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_serving  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.sampling.sampling_params import SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.server_args import (  # noqa: E402
+    ServerArgs,
+    set_global_server_args_for_scheduler,
+)
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=6, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+POOL = 128
+PROMPT = 8
+EARLIER_OUTPUT = list(range(100, 106))  # generated before the retraction
+AFTER = 3  # decode steps after the re-prefill
+
+
+class _RetractionCase(CustomTestCase):
+    PAGE = 1
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(
+            ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", page_size=self.PAGE)
+        )
+        # The server runs with the flag on, so the re-prefill sees it too.
+        stack = contextlib.ExitStack()
+        self.addCleanup(stack.close)
+        stack.enter_context(get_serving().override(strip_thinking_cache=True))
+        self._build()
+
+    def _build(self):
+        self.pool = ReqToTokenPool(
+            size=4, max_context_len=64, device="cpu", enable_memory_saver=False
+        )
+        kvcache = MHATokenToKVPool(
+            size=POOL,
+            page_size=self.PAGE,
+            dtype=torch.float16,
+            head_num=1,
+            head_dim=8,
+            layer_num=1,
+            device="cpu",
+            enable_memory_saver=False,
+        )
+        if self.PAGE == 1:
+            self.allocator = TokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+                size=POOL,
+                dtype=torch.float16,
+                device="cpu",
+                kvcache=kvcache,
+                need_sort=False,
+            )
+        else:
+            self.allocator = PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+                size=POOL,
+                page_size=self.PAGE,
+                dtype=torch.float16,
+                device="cpu",
+                kvcache=kvcache,
+                need_sort=False,
+            )
+        self.cache = UnifiedRadixCache(
+            params=CacheInitParams(
+                req_to_token_pool=self.pool,
+                token_to_kv_pool_allocator=self.allocator,
+                page_size=self.PAGE,
+                disable=False,
+                tree_components=(ComponentType.FULL,),
+            )
+        )
+        self.page_tail = []  # unused slots of the row's last page
+
+    def _slots(self, n):
+        # Whole pages per row, so no two rows share a page.
+        while len(self.page_tail) < n:
+            self.page_tail += self.allocator.alloc(self.PAGE).tolist()
+        slots, self.page_tail = self.page_tail[:n], self.page_tail[n:]
+        return torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    def _admit(self, prompt, output, reasoning=True):
+        """Match prompt + output and lock the hit, as admission does."""
+        req = Req(
+            f"r-{len(output)}-{reasoning}",
+            "",
+            array("q", range(1, prompt + 1)),
+            SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_new_tokens=32),
+        )
+        req.output_ids = array("q", output)
+        req.reasoning_tokens = len(output) + 1 if reasoning else 0
+        req.extra_key = None
+        req.init_next_round_input(self.cache)
+        req.lock = self.cache.lock(req.last_node)
+        prefix = self.cache.prefix_device_indices(req)
+        self.pool.alloc([req])
+        self.pool.write(
+            (req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(0, req.prefix_len)), prefix.to(torch.int32)
+        )
+        req.kv.kv_committed_len = req.kv.kv_allocated_len = req.prefix_len
+        return req
+
+    def _extend(self, req, end):
+        req.extend_end = end
+        self.pool.write(
+            (req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(req.prefix_len, end)),
+            self._slots(end - req.prefix_len),
+        )
+        req.kv.kv_committed_len = req.kv.kv_allocated_len = end
+
+    def _prefill_and_decode(self, req, chunk_end=None):
+        """Prefill prompt + output (a re-prefill when output is non-empty),
+        checkpoint it as the scheduler does, then decode AFTER tokens."""
+        if chunk_end is not None:
+            self._extend(req, chunk_end)
+            checkpoint_kv_cache(req, self.cache)  # stash_chunked_request
+        self._extend(req, len(req.full_untruncated_fill_ids))
+        checkpoint_kv_cache(req, self.cache)  # batch_result_processor, unfinished
+        for _ in range(AFTER):
+            self.pool.write(
+                (req.kv.req_pool_idx, req.kv.kv_committed_len), self._slots(1)
+            )
+            req.kv.kv_committed_len += 1
+            req.kv.kv_allocated_len += 1
+            req.output_ids.append(99)
+        return req
+
+    def _release(self, req, finish):
+        if finish:
+            req.finished_reason = FINISH_LENGTH(length=len(req.output_ids))
+        release_kv_cache(req, self.cache, checkpoint=finish)
+        self.page_tail = []  # freed with the row's last page
+
+    def _release_and_check(self, req, finish):
+        tree_slots = set(
+            self.pool.req_to_token[
+                req.kv.req_pool_idx, : req.kv.cache_protected_len
+            ].tolist()
+        )
+        self._release(req, finish)
+        if self.PAGE == 1:
+            free = self.allocator.free_pages.tolist()
+            self.assertEqual(sorted(tree_slots & set(free)), [])
+        self.cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=POOL))
+        if self.PAGE > 1:
+            self.allocator.merge_and_sort_free()
+        free = self.allocator.free_pages.tolist()
+        self.assertEqual(len(free), len(set(free)), "a KV slot is free twice")
+        self.assertEqual(self.allocator.available_size(), POOL)
+
+
+class TestStripThinkingAfterRetraction(_RetractionCase):
+    def test_finish_after_reprefill_frees_each_slot_once(self):
+        req = self._prefill_and_decode(self._admit(PROMPT, EARLIER_OUTPUT))
+        self.assertGreater(req.kv.cache_protected_len, PROMPT)
+        self._release_and_check(req, finish=True)
+
+    def test_second_retraction_frees_each_slot_once(self):
+        req = self._prefill_and_decode(self._admit(PROMPT, EARLIER_OUTPUT))
+        self._release_and_check(req, finish=False)
+
+    def test_without_retraction_output_is_still_stripped(self):
+        req = self._prefill_and_decode(self._admit(PROMPT, []))
+        self.assertEqual(req.owned_kv_len(), PROMPT)
+        self._release_and_check(req, finish=True)
+
+    def test_chunked_reprefill_frees_each_slot_once(self):
+        for finish in (True, False):
+            with self.subTest(finish=finish):
+                self._build()
+                req = self._admit(PROMPT, EARLIER_OUTPUT)
+                # The first chunk ends inside the earlier output.
+                self._prefill_and_decode(req, chunk_end=PROMPT + 2)
+                self._release_and_check(req, finish=finish)
+
+    def test_reprefill_matching_cached_output_frees_each_slot_once(self):
+        for finish in (True, False):
+            with self.subTest(finish=finish):
+                self._build()
+                # A request without reasoning cached prompt + the first output
+                # tokens, so the re-prefill's match alone passes the prompt.
+                other = self._admit(PROMPT, EARLIER_OUTPUT[:4], reasoning=False)
+                self._extend(other, PROMPT + 4)
+                self._release(other, finish=True)
+                req = self._admit(PROMPT, EARLIER_OUTPUT)
+                self.assertEqual(req.prefix_len, PROMPT + 4)
+                self._prefill_and_decode(req)
+                self._release_and_check(req, finish=finish)
+
+
+class TestStripThinkingAfterRetractionPaged(_RetractionCase):

+
+    def test_reprefill_release_frees_each_page_once(self):
+        for prompt in (8, 10):  # page-aligned, unaligned
+            for finish in (True, False):
+                with self.subTest(prompt=prompt, finish=finish):
+                    self._build()
+                    req = self._admit(prompt, EARLIER_OUTPUT)
+                    self._prefill_and_decode(req)
+                    self.assertGreater(req.kv.cache_protected_len, prompt)
+                    self._release_and_check(req, finish=finish)

issue_comments.body: Thanks for porting and running it, @ischencheng. I'm moving the tests to current main and will push the merge and answer the cap question in detail.

I merged main (no force-push) and ported the tests to `checkpoint_kv_cache`, `release_kv_cache(checkpoint=...)` and `TreeLock`, with the flag on for the whole request. On CPU I get the same result as you: without the fix the finish case trips the `cache_protected_len` assert and a second retraction frees [9..14]; with it, all pass. I also added a chunked re-prefill and a re-prefill whose match already passes the prompt.

You're right that thinking tokens shouldn't stay cached after a re-prefill, and with the original four tests the cap does pass, as you found. I'll add it as a follow-up. On its own it can't replace the floor, though: when the match already passes the prompt (now one of the tests), a capped `up_to` below `cache_protected_len` trips the same assert. On a mamba tree it can key the post-thinking state under the prompt.

The cap is built, as one commit on top of this branch, with a test. With `--strip-thinking-cache` and `reasoning_tokens > 0`, `checkpoint_kv_cache` now stops a re-prefill's checkpoint at the prompt, so the earlier thinking and answer tokens no longer go into the tree:

```python
up_to = req.extend_end
if (
    get_serving().strip_thinking_cache
    and req.reasoning_tokens > 0
    and not tree_cache.supports_mamba()
):
    up_to = min(up_to, max(len(req.origin_input_ids), req.kv.cache_protected_len))
```

The new case re-prefills a retracted request, plain and chunked, and checks that nothing past the prompt is matchable: on this PR's head it fails with `14 != 8`, and with the cap the file gives 7 passed, 10 subtests passed. The floor in `owned_kv_len()` stays: when the re-prefill's match already passes the prompt, the cap can't go below `cache_protected_len`, and with the cap but without the floor that case still trips the assert on finish (`cache_protected_len=12, len(new_indices)=8`) and a second retraction frees tree slots [9..12]. It skips mamba trees, where the live recurrent state is the state after the whole re-prefill: on CPU, a capped checkpoint stores that post-thinking state under the prompt node once the node's own state has been evicted. The branch is `sohom-cs:fix/strip-thinking-cap-reprefill-checkpoint`. I'll open it as a follow-up PR once this one merges, or push it here if you'd rather review both together.
